## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāukkusajātaka* (Ja 486) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection. According to its opening frame (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha recounted the story while dwelling at Jetavana concerning a lay follower named Mittagandhaka [Fausböll 1887]. The past narrative exemplifies the theme of devoted friendship and loving-kindness (*mitta* / *mettā*) among animals who assist, shelter, and make sacrifices to protect one another in times of distress [Sahni 2008].

**Sources**

- [Sahni 2008] Pragati Sahni, Environmental Ethics in Buddhism: A Virtues Approach (2008) — Discussed the narrative's themes of animal friendship, sacrifice, mutual protection, and their ethical relevance.
- [Fausböll 1887] Viggo Fausböll (ed.), The Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 4 (1887) — Provided the nineteenth-century PTS edition text and confirmation of the introductory frame about Mittagandhaka.
